transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... look, everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. It started with my stuff. My tools don’t move themselves, you know? I’m a fabricator, been doing assembly work since I got out of high school, and if you don't keep your station organized, you lose a finger or you lose your job. My old foreman, guy named Mike, he used to walk the floor with this clipboard and just stare at you until you cleaned up your scraps... 

But anyway, it's not just the tools. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend. I was supposed to go down to the lake last Saturday. Caught a beautiful bass there a few years back, fought me for a good ten minutes, best day I've had in a long time. The weather was supposed to be perfect for it, too. But after all these months... I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, or other drugs recently—say, in the past few months or weeks?

No, no, I don't touch any of that. No drugs, no drinking. You can't be doing that kind of stuff when you're working with heavy machinery. I mean, you need a clear head to run a press brake or you're asking for trouble. 

I had a buddy, Dave, back in the late nineties, who came in smelling like a brewery one morning. Foreman sent him packing before he even punched his card. Dave was a good guy, though, just had a rough patch. He had this old Chevy C10 he was restoring in his garage. Beautiful truck, cherry red. We used to drive out to these swap meets in the county on the weekends looking for original parts. You wouldn't believe the absolute junk people try to sell you at those things, just boxes of rusted bolts and they want top dollar for it. We walked around for hours in the baking sun one time just looking for a specific door handle... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right. No, I haven't been drinking or taking anything.
When you say your wife's relative is trying to push you out of your place, is there any possibility at all that you could be wrong about that, or are you completely certain that's what's happening?

Wrong? No. No, there is zero possibility I'm wrong. Everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it, but I *know* my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I am completely certain of it. 

Like I said, my tools don’t move themselves. You know how much a good set of calipers costs these days? I use Mitutoyo, the digital ones. When you're fabricating, you need that exact precision. A fraction of a millimeter off and the whole assembly won't fit into the housing. We had this young kid on the line once, maybe twenty years old, who dropped his calipers and didn't say anything. Ruined a whole batch of aluminum brackets. The foreman was so red in the face I thought he was gonna have a heart attack right there on the shop floor. They had to scrap like two thousand dollars worth of material. Aluminum ain't cheap, especially the aircraft-grade stuff. They used to mine a lot of it up north, but now it's mostly imported, you know? Shipping costs are just through the roof these days. You go to the hardware store and a simple piece of flashing costs you double what it did five years ago... 

But anyway, what I'm saying is, it's all connected. My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend either. It's all deliberate. After all these months, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. I'm not wrong about this, Doc. I see exactly what he's doing.
Besides noticing that your tools have moved and your fishing plans getting spoiled, have you heard any voices or seen anything unusual that other people around you couldn't hear or see?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and eyesight are perfectly fine. Better than most guys my age, actually. You have to have good ears in the shop, you know? You learn to listen to the machines. I can hear when a bearing is starting to go bad on a press before the digital sensors even pick it up. It makes this real subtle whining sound, kind of like... well, kind of like the transmission on my brother-in-law's old Ford Taurus. 

He drove that thing into the ground. Never changed the fluid once. I told him, I said, you gotta maintain your equipment or it's gonna leave you stranded. Sure enough, we were driving up to the state park for a camping trip back in... must have been '04, '05 maybe? Middle of July, hotter than blazes, and the thing just locked up on the highway. We had to sit on the shoulder for three hours waiting for a tow. The guy who finally showed up was eating a meatball sub right there in the cab, got sauce all over the steering wheel. I couldn't believe it. You gotta have respect for your vehicle, you know? It's like a tool. You take care of it, it takes care of you. People just don't have pride in their things anymore. They buy cheap plastic junk and throw it away when it breaks. 

But anyway... what was the question? Did I hear something? No, no voices or anything crazy like that. Just the regular sounds. I just see what's actually happening right in front of me, that's all.
You mentioned your wife's relative is behind this. Can you tell me his name and describe exactly what you've seen him do or how you know he's been in your house?

His name? Well... you know, her family is just huge. Massive. They're mostly from out near the state line, and there's so many cousins and second cousins I can't keep them all straight. We went to a family reunion out there back in, oh, 2012 maybe? Rented out this whole pavilion by the lake. Beautiful spot, but the mosquitoes were just murder. Big as quarters, I swear. My wife's aunt brought this potato salad that sat out in the sun for like four hours. I told her, I said, you can't leave mayonnaise out in ninety-degree heat, but nobody listens to me. Half the family got sick. I was fine, though, because I stuck to the burgers. You gotta cook the meat all the way through, you know? Some of these guys, they flip it once and call it done. That's how you get E. coli. 

We had a guy at the shop who got E. coli from a food truck down the street. He was out for a week and a half. Boss was furious because we were behind on a big order for John Deere. You know they paint all their stuff that specific green? It's trademarked. You can't just go buy John Deere green off the shelf at the hardware store. They have a whole proprietary mixing process for the paint booths. If you don't clean the nozzles on the sprayers right after using it, it gums up the whole line and you're out there with a wire brush for three hours...

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right. Her relative. Look, I don't know his exact name right this second, there's just too many of them to keep track of. And I haven't caught him on camera or anything yet. But I know it's one of them. I just know.

You mentioned you know it's one of your wife's relatives doing this, but you can't quite remember which one. Has there been a specific person—someone whose name you do know—that you've suspected most of all, or do you think it could be any number of different people from her family?

Well, I don't... I don't have a specific name, no. I mean, it could be any of them. Like I said, her family is just massive. You go to one of those reunions and it's just a sea of people. And they all kind of look alike, you know? They've all got that same kind of square jaw. My wife's got it too, a little bit. It's a strong feature. 

You know, speaking of strong features, we were working on this custom chassis last month for a guy who races dirt tracks. He wanted the whole frame reinforced with chromoly tubing. Chromoly is tough stuff, let me tell you. You can't just weld it like regular mild steel, you gotta pre-heat it and then TIG weld it, otherwise the joints get brittle and they'll snap right off when you hit a bump at eighty miles an hour. I've been TIG welding for... oh, gotta be going on twenty-five years now. My hands are still steady as a rock. You gotta have a steady hand, and you gotta control your breathing. It's almost like being a sniper, you know? You get in the zone, under the hood, and it's just you and the puddle of metal. Sometimes I'll be under there for hours and I won't even realize the guys have all gone to lunch. 

They usually go down to this deli on 4th Street. Good pastrami, but they charge an arm and a leg. I always pack my own lunch. You save a lot of money that way, and you know exactly what you're eating. I got this insulated thermos that keeps my soup hot until 2 PM. Best twenty bucks I ever spent... 

But yeah, no, I don't have one specific name for you. It's just one of them. I know it is.

When you think about who's been moving your tools and ruining your fishing trips, do you have even one person in mind—someone whose face you can picture—or is it really just a feeling that it's someone from your wife's family without being able to think of any specific person at all?

A face? Well, I don't need to picture a specific face to know what's happening right under my nose. I mean, speaking of faces and pictures, my wife bought one of those digital picture frames for the living room a while back. You know the ones? You plug a little memory card into the side and it just flips through family photos all day long. It's supposed to be nice, but the screen on that thing is so bright it glares right off the TV screen. I tried to take the back off it last week to wire in a resistor, just to dim the LED backlight a little bit. 

You gotta be real careful with those modern circuit boards, though. The surface-mount components are tiny. You sneeze with a soldering iron in your hand and you've bridged three pins and fried the whole thing. I used to do a lot of small electronic repair back in the nineties when things were actually built to be fixed. Now? They pot everything in epoxy. They don't want you fixing your own stuff, they just want you to throw it in the trash and buy a new one. It's a total racket, is what it is. 

But anyway... look, I’m only here talking to you because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. They act like I'm making it all up in my head. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I don't need a name or a mugshot to know that. My tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! It's deliberate. And after all these months of dealing with this, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. It's obvious if you just look at the facts.

When you think about everything that's been happening—your tools moving, your fishing trips being ruined—do you believe it's definitely one specific person doing all of it, or do you think it could be multiple different people from her family working together?

Working together? Well... I mean, maybe? But like I just said, I know it's *him*. Her relative. If he's got help, well, they're a lot more coordinated than the guys on my floor, I'll tell you that. 

Speaking of working together, you should see the new guys they just hired at the shop. Total disaster. They don't even know how to read a basic schematic. We were supposed to be assembling this heavy-duty dual-axle trailer last Tuesday, right? And this kid, he couldn't have been more than nineteen, starts bolting the leaf springs on backward. I told him, I said, 'Buddy, you're gonna have a blowout before this thing even hits the highway.' You gotta pay attention to the load distribution. If the weight isn't centered over the axles, the whole trailer starts swaying. I saw a guy flip a Ford F-250 on the interstate once because he loaded a pallet of cinder blocks at the very back of his trailer instead of over the wheels. Just fishtailed right into the ditch. Took out a speed limit sign, a mile marker, the whole nine yards. State troopers had to shut down two lanes for a tow truck... 

But anyway, look. Whether he's got his cousins helping him or not, I already told you what's going on. Everyone keeps looking at me like I'm imagining things, but I'm not crazy. I know her relative came into my house to get at me. My wrenches don't just grow legs and walk away, and my fishing plans don't just magically get ruined every single weekend by coincidence. After all these months of dealing with this, it's plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place and push me right out of my own life.

I want to make sure I understand this clearly: when you say your wife's relative is doing this, do you have any sense at all of which specific person it might be—even if you're not completely certain—or is it truly that it could be any one of them with no particular person coming to mind more than the others?

I feel like a broken record here, Doc. We keep going in circles. I don't have a specific name for you, it could be any of them. But it doesn't matter what his name is, what matters is what he's doing. 

Just the other day, I went to grab my digital caliper off my workbench. It’s a Mitutoyo. You can't just buy those at the local hardware store, they cost a pretty penny and they're accurate to the thousandth of an inch. You gotta keep 'em in their padded case, too, so the dust doesn't mess up the slide. Dust in a fabrication shop is no joke, let me tell you. We got aluminum dust, steel shavings... you breathe that stuff in for twenty years and your lungs end up looking like a Brillo pad. OSHA actually came down on our shop a few years back because the ventilation system wasn't pulling enough CFM. They made the owner install these massive overhead extractors. Thing sounded like a 747 jet engine running all day long. Gave me a splitting headache until I finally started wearing those heavy-duty earmuffs the guys on the tarmac use... 

But anyway, my caliper was gone. Moved entirely. And look, I keep telling you this—I’m only sitting in this chair right now because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it all. They treat me like I'm making it up. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! It’s been happening for months, and I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out of my own life. I don't need to know his birth certificate to see what's right in front of my face.

If you had to point to one person right now—even if you're not 100% sure—who do you think is most likely the one doing this to you? Is there anyone from her family who comes to mind first, or is it truly impossible for you to narrow it down to even one person?

Narrow it down? Doc, I honestly can't point a finger at just one of 'em. It's impossible to narrow it down. 

Speaking of narrowing things down, though, you should try narrowing down the tolerances on a quarter-inch steel plate when the shop's plasma cutter is running hot. We had this massive order of custom brackets for a commercial HVAC unit last month, right? And the client wanted everything within a sixteenth of an inch. A sixteenth! I told the foreman, I said, 'Jim, you want precision like that, you need a waterjet or a laser cutter, not this old plasma rig.' But Jim is a total cheapskate. Always trying to cut corners to save a buck. He buys these cheap off-brand copper nozzles from overseas, and they slag up after barely two hours of cutting. So then you have to spend half your shift just grinding off the dross with an angle grinder. My shoulders were absolutely screaming by Friday. You ever run a four-and-a-half-inch Makita grinder for eight hours straight? Your hands go completely numb. The vibration just destroys your nerves, wakes you up in the middle of the night tingling... 

But anyway, look, I feel like I'm beating a dead horse here. I'm only sitting here talking to you about this because everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it. They all think I'm crazy. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I don't need a name tag to prove it. My tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! It’s been happening for months, and I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. That's the truth, whether I can give you a first and last name or not.

When your tools go missing or your fishing plans fall through, have you actually seen your wife's relative in your house, or found any physical evidence like fingerprints, or is it more that you've figured out it must be him based on how things add up?

Seen him? Fingerprints? No, I haven't dusted my garage for prints like I'm some detective on TV. I just figured it out because of how it all adds up. 

Though, speaking of fingerprints, you have any idea what a nightmare it is to get skin oils off raw stainless steel? When we fabricate those commercial kitchen prep tables at the shop, you can't leave a single smudge on the 304 stainless. The restaurant owners go ballistic. You gotta wipe the whole thing down with acetone before it ever gets loaded on the truck. And you have to wear these thick nitrile gloves to keep your hands clean, but the gloves are a massive safety hazard if you're working near the rotating machinery. I had a buddy, Frank, who got his glove snagged in a belt sander back in '98. Ripped his thumb clean out of the socket. The screaming... man, I'll never forget that sound echoing over the shop floor. We had to pack his hand in a Styrofoam cooler from the breakroom just for the ambulance ride. Took the surgeons like six hours to reattach it, and he still can't bend it past forty-five degrees...

But anyway, like I've been trying to explain to you, I don't need to see his literal thumbprints on my workbench to know what's happening. I’m only sitting here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it all, but I know for a fact my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. Look, my tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! After all these months of dealing with this garbage, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. You just don't need a magnifying glass when the writing is on the wall.

If your wife sat down with you right now and showed you proof—like security camera footage—that nobody from her family had been in your house and your tools were where you left them, would that change your mind about what's been happening, or would you still believe he's behind it somehow?

Change my mind? A video? Look, Doc, cameras can be tampered with. He could just loop the feed or find a blind spot. I'd still know he was behind it. 

Actually, speaking of security cameras, you wouldn't believe the cheap junk they sell these days. The owner at the fabrication shop bought this eight-channel system off the internet last year because guys were supposedly stealing copper scrap from the bins out back. Copper prices have been insane lately, right? Bare bright wire was fetching over four bucks a pound at the yard. I used to save up my own off-cuts in a five-gallon bucket in my garage, take it down to the scrap yard right before Christmas to get a little extra cash for presents. The guy at the scale, this old guy named Earl, he always tried to short me on the tare weight of the bucket. You gotta watch those scrap yard guys like a hawk. I swear, they'll zero the scale with their foot resting on the corner if you aren't paying attention. I finally had to start weighing my buckets on my own bathroom scale before I drove down there just to keep him honest...

But anyway, what was I... right, the footage. Look, I feel like a broken record, but I am only here because everybody, my wife included, keeps acting like I’m imagining it all. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. A camera doesn't change that. My tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! After all these months of this happening, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. Video or no video, I know what's happening in my own home.

If multiple people you trust completely—your wife, your boss, maybe a family member—all sat down together and told you they had watched your house 24/7 for an entire week and confirmed that nobody from her family ever came inside, would that be enough to make you reconsider whether someone is actually coming into your house, or would you still be certain it's happening no matter what they said?

Reconsider? Doc, nobody can actually watch a place 24/7 without blinking or looking away. I'd still be absolutely certain he's getting in. 

You know, speaking of 24/7, you ever try working a rotating swing shift? Back in '06, the fabrication plant got this massive government contract for aluminum chassis, and they had us running three shifts, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. I was stuck on the graveyard shift, 11 PM to 7 AM. It completely destroys your internal clock. You're trying to sleep at noon with the sun blazing, and the neighbor's kid is out there revving a two-stroke lawnmower. I bought these heavy blackout curtains, but they always leave that little gap at the edge where the light shoots in like a laser beam right into your eyeball. And the food... man, you end up eating gas station hot dogs at 3 in the morning because nothing else is open. My cholesterol went through the roof that year. I was eating those roller-grill taquitos every night, and the acid reflux was just brutal. You ever try welding overhead when your stomach is on fire? It's miserable...

But anyway, what I'm saying is, it doesn't matter who sits down with me or what they claim they saw. I’m only here in this office because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. My own wife, my boss, whoever—they all treat me like I'm making it up. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. They can swear up and down they watched the place, but my tools don’t move themselves! My fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend! After all these months of this happening, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out, and no little week-long stakeout is gonna change the facts.
